title: T-Bone Walker and Booker Pittman in Dallas
summary: Gus remembers T-Bone Walker as a rougher, faster-living older kid with a guitar, and mentions saxophonist Booker Pittman, whom he later saw in South America.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Ten minutes. Well, then, let's talk about -- because, you see, you were there in that time and
quite a lot of different people that we all know, I think, -- one was T-Bone Walker.
T-Bone Walker.
Because you and T-Bone were born the same year.
Right.
And he lived in South Dallas, I guess.
Right.
But at the same time, he must have gone to Booker T. Washington.
I'm trying to --
It was the only high school.
I'm trying to --
You said you remember running into T-Bone here and there, but he seemed like he was a little bit older boy that you. He was a --
To me, he was a rougher kid that I was, and he was much maturer to me.
Yeah, he kept a little fast company maybe.
Oh, yeah, much faster company.
Because he was a gambler. T-Bone liked to gamble all the time.
That's right, that's right.
From the time he was very young.
He was up there, Thomas and Hall, there, they used to have gambling places all along there.
OH, did they?
The dance hall, what was that, Booker's? Even Booker Pittman.
Really?
Yeah, he was a saxophone player.
Oh, was he? Yeah.
He died a pretty good while back. He left Dallas and went to South America.
Oh, did he?
I saw him in South America.
Really? What a funny thing.
Yeah. He remembered me.
Did he?
Yeah.
Well, isn't the one who used to talk about going out to the golf course or the golf club, where he said all the different kids would caddy and also shoot dice.
Well, I never went to the golf course.
Oh, you didn't?
No, see, that's the reason I said --
He was different company.
Different company altogether.
Well, anyway, by the fact of him being
a guitar player, and from early on, he would have been earning money on guitar at that time.
Oh, yes, that's right. He used to go around -- you'd see him all the time with his guitar.
You would?
You sure would.
